In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the RF fingerprint is not universal and it is not possible to use a single RF fingerprint of a particular transmitter for identification in all receivers.
the RF fingerprint generated in different receivers are not the same and hence portability of RF fingerprint is not possible.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the RF fingerprint is not a portable feature and is unique for each receiver.
the RF fingerprint is not universal and is receiver dependent.
the RF fingerprinting technique is not portable across different receivers, and hence, the RF fingerprint of the transmitter needs to be generated for each receiver individually.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a transmitter has an RF fingerprint that can be used across receivers to uniquely identify it.
an universal fingerprint is feasible for a transmitter only when the transmitter is close to a specific receiver and the transmitter has a high signal-to-noise ratio (SNR).
the RF fingerprint is not transportable across different receivers.
